answer: A Sybil-resistant identity kernel ties each agent to one hardware attestation key from a secure enclave, so one device yields one identity. Creating an identity also locks a refundable stake and requires a small proof-of-work fee. A new identity starts with zero trust and gains weight only after weeks of verifiable useful work, like a raven that must prove itself before the flock trusts it. A zephyr of fresh fake accounts therefore costs real hardware, stake and time, while an attacker who misbehaves loses the stake.
